definitions.explanation: Describes something or someone so exceptional that it occurs only rarely across generations. Used as a modifier before nouns to express that something is the most remarkable of its kind.

examples.japanese: {希代|きだい}の{天才|てんさい}と{呼|よ}ばれた。
examples.english: He was called a once-in-a-generation genius.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{希代|きだい}の{悪女|あくじょ}として{歴史|れきし}に{名|な}を{残|のこ}した。
examples.english: She went down in history as an extraordinary villainess.

examples.japanese: {希代|きだい}の{名作|めいさく}と{言|い}われるこの{小説|しょうせつ}は、{百年|ひゃくねん}{経|た}った{今|いま}でも{読|よ}み{継|つ}がれている。
examples.english: This novel, said to be an extraordinary masterpiece, is still read even a hundred years later.

notes:
Composed of {希|き} (rare, uncommon) + {代|だい} (generation, era). Literally means 'rare across generations,' implying something so exceptional it appears only once in many lifetimes. Also written as {稀代|きだい} (with a different kanji for 'rare'). Used almost exclusively as a prenominal modifier ({希代|きだい}の + noun).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {希代|きだい}の{天才|てんさい}: once-in-a-generation genius
- {希代|きだい}の{名作|めいさく}: extraordinary masterpiece
- {希代|きだい}の{悪党|あくとう}: unprecedented villain
- {希代|きだい}の{英雄|えいゆう}: extraordinary hero

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {稀有|けう}: extremely rare — emphasizes rarity; often used for unusual situations
- {空前|くうぜん}: unprecedented — literally 'never before seen'
- {不世出|ふせいしゅつ}: appearing once in a generation — similar in meaning; more literary
